title: RISE Live: the ask bar at the room's foot
acceptance: In the room (once a question has been asked), bottom to top: the stage's instrument (transport row and passage ticks), the ask bar 8 px above it, a line kept for the bar's note, the spoken words' two lines, then the face's square; nothing overlaps at 1440x900 or 390x844, in the eye, the shell and the full frame, collapsed while it plays and open while an interjection is typed. The entry before a question is unchanged and has no bar.

One geometry: roomLayout (src/live/host/frames.js) computes the bar's place, the words' foot and size, the face's square, the dock and the full frame's safe rectangle from the instrument's top, the bar's box, its note and the keyboard; the venue only measures those and sets --live-bar-foot, --live-words-foot and --live-words-size, which LiveHost.css reads.

In the full frame the face docks 48 px wide within 40 px of the bar's left end, centred on the bar and wholly on screen; a fitted figure or generated scene lies between the room's top (12 px below the corner's sign-in link) and 12 px above the words' zone; the words lie above the bar.

On a phone, while the bar's field has focus, an on-screen keyboard reaching above the bar's place lifts the bar to 8 px above it (window.visualViewport), the words above the bar; it comes down when the field loses focus. Emulated in Playwright with a reduced visualViewport height; a real iPhone or Android keyboard is unverified until seen on a device.
At 390x844 the corner's "Staff sign in" link no longer meets the bar; the rule that hid it while the bar was open is gone.

Every existing behaviour is kept: an interjection typed into the bar holds the reading, the microphone, the bar's note line, Ask again and Leave, reduced motion, focus order and screen-reader labels; the Settings sheet opens whole over the bar.

evidence.note: The owner's approved study: the ask bar at the room's foot with Sophia's slot at its left end, the words above it.
§23 The three frames: the ask bar at the foot (the stack, one layout function, the keyboard, the Settings sheet over the bar), the words above the bar, the safe rectangle below the corner's link.

Branch live-ask-bar-bottom. Command: npx vitest run src/live/host src/core/rise-sdk.test.js src/live/boundary.test.js src/scenes/engines/oracle.test.js src/core/system-design.test.js src/live/catalog-words.test.js src/live/runtime.catalog.test.js: 20 files, 647 passed. roomLayout at 1440x900 (instrument from 820: bar top 758, foot 88, words foot 174, dock 400,785) and 390x844 (instrument from 776: bar top 714, foot 76, dock 40,741, wholly on screen), a 336 px keyboard (bar foot 344), a two-line note, no bar; the venue sets --live-bar-foot and --live-words-foot, has no bar before a question, and lifts the bar over an emulated visual viewport while its field has focus.

Branch live-ask-bar-bottom, local production build, headless Chromium. Command: npx playwright test e2e/live.spec.js -g "the frames|the face rests|catalog words|remembers the room|interactive scenes|the interjection|the ask bar|asks, reads under the whole instrument": 16 passed. The bar below the words and above the instrument at 1440x900 and 390x844, open while an interjection is typed; the full-frame face within 40 px of the bar's left end, centred on it; the fitted figure between the top and the words; the sign-in link clear of the bar at 390x844; the bar above an emulated 336 px keyboard (visualViewport height reduced) and back down on blur. A real iPhone or Android keyboard is unverified.

Renders by the agent (not a human observation), kept by the coordinator: bar-eye, bar-shell, bar-full-figure, bar-full-field, bar-interjection, bar-note at 1440x900 and 390x844, and bar-keyboard-390 (an emulated keyboard drawn in grey). Bottom to top: instrument, bar, note line, words, the face's square; nothing overlaps. Not accepted by a human.

summary: In RISE Live's room the ask bar sits at the foot, above the stage's instrument (or an on-screen keyboard), with Sophia docked at its left end in the full frame and the spoken words above it, as in the approved study; the entry is unchanged.
